rationale:
D11 layer 1 shipped symbol BODIES and is live and proven (bodies 4,535/4,535 at the time, 4,992 now; the contract's own '%stop_reason%' example went 0 -> 6 hits). bugs_open/108 is CLOSED, both defects. So seats can now read what the CODE does.

They still cannot read a single word of PROSE. Measured on the live index today: 0 of 4,992 rows are markdown. That means WRONG_CALLS.md, /bugs_open/, /bugs_closed/ and 016b are invisible to every council seat and to the diagnosis loop's code tier. Those four files are the platform's entire written record of HOW WE GET THINGS WRONG, and the seats whose charter is policing claims of absence and repetition cannot see them.

This workstream has its own evidence that the gap is load-bearing, and it is uncomfortable: on 2026-07-27 prior_art_librarian rejected an absence claim in MY OWN council submission by citing the code index, one hour after I had wired that seat up to it. The same day, a different submission of mine proposed extracting a shared line-slicer that already existed forty lines below a line I had cited twice. In both cases a reviewer WITH the record in front of it caught what the author of that record had missed the same day. The record it could not see is the markdown one.

OWNER-SCOPED, 2026-07-28: index the FOUR DURABLE SOURCES only -- bugs_open + bugs_closed, WRONG_CALLS.md, 016b, and the concept register. NOT all of docs024. That is a deliberate exclusion, not an oversight: docs024 holds 1,415 .md files, most of them handoffs, NOTES and summaries which are SUPERSEDED BY DESIGN. A reviewer citing a stale handoff as evidence is precisely the failure this workstream exists to prevent, so indexing them would arm the failure rather than the fix. The four sources are append-only or curated; their value grows rather than decays.

EVERY PRECONDITION BELOW WAS RUN, NOT ASSUMED. The last plan this workstream submitted was APPROVED by twelve seats while asserting 'the indexer is already walking the file' -- it was not; it walks a JSON-decoded analysis.Output with no source text in it, and the sketch sliced bytes out of a `fileSrc` that existed nowhere in scope. It worked only because live config had been changed in a way the repo's own seed still does not reflect. So the load-bearing precondition here was checked FIRST: analyse_repo_local calls src.FetchToDir at line 165 (whole tarball, unfiltered) and analysis.AnalyseWithExclude at line 197 (filters the ANALYSIS only), and defaultAnalyseExcludePatterns is []string{"docs/"} -- an ANALYSER-time exclude. Therefore docs/ IS present on disk in the indexer pod and can be walked. If that had been a fetch-time exclude this plan would be impossible, and nothing in the plan would have said so.

plan.summary: D11 layer 1b: index MARKDOWN sections from the four durable prose sources into code_symbols, reusing the body column and the content-search path layer 1 built. One section per heading: symbol = the heading, body = the section text, kind = a new 'doc'. Requires relaxing the code_symbols_kind_check CHECK, which today permits Go kinds only. Measured scope: ~1,749 sections against 4,992 existing rows (+35%). Deliberately does NOT index the other 1,415 docs024 files.

edits.rationale: code_symbols.kind carries a CHECK permitting Go kinds ONLY, so a markdown row cannot be inserted at all -- this is the mechanical blocker, not a preference. Verbatim from the live DB: CHECK ((kind = ANY (ARRAY['func'::text, 'method'::text, 'struct'::text, 'interface'::text, 'alias'::text, 'type'::text, 'var'::text, 'const'::text]))). Adds 'doc'. NUMBER MOVES: 253 is the highest today, but on 2026-07-27 this workstream's migration was approved as 241 and shipped as 243 because two sessions took 241 and 242 inside four hours -- guardian objected then that 'the next free number' is an assertion no SQL can check, and was vindicated twice. Re-read `ls docs/agent_docs/sql_for_agents/*.sql | xargs -n1 basename | grep -oE '^[0-9]+' | sort -n | tail -1` immediately before writing the file.

Produce one symbolRow per markdown heading-section, from the checkout the indexer already has. Reuses symbolRow unchanged, so the existing upsert, prune, embed-on-hash-change and body handling all apply with no second write path -- there is exactly ONE live writer of code_symbols (verified: grep -rln 'INSERT INTO code_symbols' --include=*.go returns one file), and this keeps it that way. IDENTITY: uq_code_symbols_identity is (repo, path, symbol), so two identical headings in ONE file would collide and the second would silently overwrite the first. Measured, not assumed: WRONG_CALLS.md has 212 headings of which 211 are unique (1 collision); 016b has 130, all unique. Rare but real, so the collision is disambiguated rather than hoped away.

content does THREE jobs -- trigram text, the EMBEDDED text, and the input to content_hash which is the re-embed trigger. For code, composeSymbolContent puts kind + symbol + signature + doc + path in it and the BODY is deliberately kept out; folding bodies in would silently re-embed the whole table. Markdown must obey the same rule or the first reindex re-embeds all 4,992 existing rows plus the new ones. So content is heading + path only, and the section text goes to body.

Append the markdown rows to the Go rows before the existing upsert/prune loop, so both kinds share one commit_sha, one prune and one set of counters. The prune (DELETE WHERE repo=$1 AND commit_sha IS DISTINCT FROM $2) then covers markdown automatically -- a section deleted from a file disappears on the next index, with no second reaper to keep in step. Reports doc counts separately in the result so a run that indexed code and no prose is legible from the orchestration record, which is how the with_body=0 case was made visible in layer 1.

The owner scoped this to four sources on 2026-07-28 and the exclusion is the load-bearing half. docs024 holds 1,415 .md files, overwhelmingly handoffs/NOTES/summaries that are superseded by design; a seat citing a stale handoff as evidence is the exact failure this workstream exists to prevent. Default lives in Go (single source of truth) and is config-overridable per step, matching how defaultAnalyseExcludePatterns is done in analyse_repo_local_action.go:285.

Ships the assertions as code rather than asking a reviewer to look, which is what 243's VERIFY established for layer 1 and what caught a real defect there. UPPERCASE sidecars are recognised by run-migrations.sh SIDECAR_RE as not-a-migration, so this is re-runnable. Note the 243 lesson: a VERIFY pinned to the OLD implementation reports on a query nobody runs while presenting as coverage -- 243's check 5 had to be corrected after the predicate changed.
edits.sketch:
-- 1. the code invariant must survive: no row's content_hash may include its body
SELECT count(*) AS hash_drift FROM code_symbols
 WHERE content_hash IS DISTINCT FROM encode(sha256(convert_to(content,'UTF8')),'hex');  -- expect 0
-- 2. markdown actually arrived, and only from the four sources
SELECT kind, count(*) FROM code_symbols GROUP BY 1;                    -- expect a 'doc' row
SELECT count(*) AS out_of_scope FROM code_symbols WHERE kind='doc'
 AND path NOT LIKE 'bugs_open/%' AND path NOT LIKE 'bugs_closed/%'
 AND path NOT LIKE '%WRONG_CALLS.md' AND path NOT LIKE '%016b_%'
 AND path NOT LIKE 'docs/agent_docs/docs026_concept_register/%';       -- expect 0
-- 3. the fix is real: a prose-only string must now be findable
SELECT count(*) AS wrongcalls_hits FROM code_symbols
 WHERE kind='doc' AND body ILIKE '%wrote-it-down-before-i-checked-it%';  -- expect > 0
SELECT count(*) AS negative_control FROM code_symbols
 WHERE body ILIKE '%zzz_string_that_appears_nowhere_zzz%';               -- expect 0
-- 4. identity collisions did not silently swallow sections
SELECT count(*) AS sections FROM code_symbols WHERE kind='doc';         -- compare to ~1,749

plan.risks: (1) THE ONE INVARIANT, unchanged from layer 1: content and content_hash must not gain the section text, or every existing row re-embeds. composeDocContent is heading+path only and the VERIFY asserts hash integrity across ALL rows, not just new ones. (2) EMBEDDING COST IS REAL AND NEW: ~1,749 new rows each embed once on first index (content is small, but the call count is not zero). Later runs re-embed only on content_hash change, and a heading rarely changes. Worth stating because layer 1's cost was zero-by-construction and this one is not. (3) IDENTITY COLLISION: measured at 1 in-file duplicate heading today; the disambiguator makes it representable rather than silent, but a reviewer should check the suffix scheme is deterministic across runs, or the row identity churns every index and the prune deletes and recreates rows needlessly. (4) SCOPE CREEP IS THE MAIN NON-TECHNICAL RISK: the globs are the whole design. Widening them to docs024/**/*.md would index 1,415 superseded handoffs and arm the exact failure -- a seat citing a stale doc as evidence -- that this workstream exists to prevent. (5) DEPLOY VERIFICATION: Go is inert until the image rolls, so the CHECK relaxes immediately and markdown simply does not arrive until then -- a degrade, not a break, and the existing scope note already reports bodies-indexed coverage. Confirm against the RUNNING pod with a string this change creates plus one it does not, never git and never the tag. (6) The freshness banner now keys on the indexed COMMIT (108 defect A, live v1.0.1189), so a prose answer carries the same staleness qualifier a code answer does -- no new honesty gap is opened by making prose searchable.
